parts.text: A student investigates the resistance of a lamp. She uses the circuit shown in Fig. 2.1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) On Fig. 2.1, draw a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference (p.d.) across the lamp. [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student places a sliding contact S on the resistance wire CE as close as possible to point C. She measures the potential difference V 1 across lamp L and the current I 1 in the circuit. The readings are shown in Fig. 2.2 and Fig. 2.3.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate the resistance R 1 of lamp L. Use the equation R 1 = V 1 I 1 . Include the unit. R 1 = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) She places the sliding contact S on the resistance wire as close as possible to point D. Point D is at the mid-point of the resistance wire. She measures the potential difference V 2 across lamp L. 1.4 V 2 = ............................................................ V She measures the current I 2 in the circuit. 0.24 I 2 = ............................................................ A Calculate the resistance R 2 of lamp L. Use the equation R 2 = V 2 I 2 . Include the unit. Give your answer to a suitable number of significant figures for this experiment. R 2 = ......................................................... [1]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) She places the sliding contact S on the resistance wire as close as possible to point E. She measures the potential difference V 3 across lamp L. 0.9 V 3 = ............................................................ V She measures the current I 3 in the circuit. 0.18 I 3 = ............................................................ A Calculate the resistance R 3 of lamp L. Use the equation R 3 = V 3 I 3 . Include the unit. R 3 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text:
R = 5(.0) with unit Ω (here or seen in (a) or (b)(ii) and not contradicted)
3

parts.label: e
parts.text: (e) Complete the following statements, referring to your practical experience and the results. 1. As the length of resistance wire included in the circuit is increased, the brightness of the lamp ................................................................................. . 2. As the length of resistance wire included in the circuit is increased, the resistance of the lamp ................................................................................. . [2]

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) A variable resistor can be used in this type of experiment in place of the resistance wire. Draw a circuit diagram to show a variable resistor in place of the resistance wire. Include the ammeter and the voltmeter in your diagram. [3]

ms.label: 2(f)
ms.text:
Correct symbol for variable resistor
Variable resistor in series with power source and ammeter
Ammeter and lamp with correct symbols and no flying lead at all
